messages:
kevin.ops: Heads up — saw a sharp ECC correctable spike on gpu-nodes in eu-west-1 over the last 18m. ~3x baseline on several cards. SRE alert fired.

sre-bot: Alert: ECC_CORRECTABLE_SPIKE (eu-west-1) • nodes: gpu-0[3], gpu-1[2], gpu-7[1] • window=18m • severity=warn

leah.sre: Thanks Kevin. Is this across a single host or spread?

kevin.ops: Spread across 4 hosts, different racks. Not all GPUs on a host. Pattern looks like per-card bursts instead of host-wide.

maria.mlinfra: Can you paste the prom query you used? want to compare to the last 7d baseline.

kevin.ops: Prom query I ran:```promql
sum by (gpu_id)(increase(nvidia_ecc_correctable_total[18m]))
/ max(1, sum by (gpu_id)(increase(nvidia_uptime_seconds[18m]) / 3600))
```
It gave a deg_rate (correctables per GPU-hour). A couple of cards hit ~420 corr/hr which is way above normal (~<20/hr).

jonathan.eng: 420/hr is nasty. Historically we've used a hard threshold of 200/hr -> immediate drain, but that caused capacity churn. We should refine to avoid noisy false positives.

leah.sre: Agree. Proposal: classify signals into three actionable bands and a circuit-breaker gating by regional spare capacity.

maria.mlinfra: Outline?

leah.sre: Band A (info): deg_rate 0-50/hr — log, tag GPU, no action.
Band B (investigate): 50-200/hr for >30m — run nvml logs, schedule a rolling probe workload, mark as suspect.
Band C (drain candidate): >200/hr sustained for 20m OR >500/hr instantaneous — auto-drain only if region spare >= 8% or if cluster in maintenance window. Otherwise mark for manual drain with high priority.

jonathan.eng: +1 on the gating. EU-west has been at 93% GPU utilization during daytime so auto-drain there would blow SLAs. We need a safe degrade policy that can be overridden by an oncall.

kevin.ops: Also add card-age and model into the decision. Older Ampere cards tend to show more correctables. We should normalize deg_rate by device_age_weeks or a rolling baseline per-model.

maria.mlinfra: Good call. So actionable metric becomes normalized_deg = deg_rate / model_median_baseline. Then thresholds are percentiles rather than absolute. That avoids over-draining older fleets.

sre-bot: Suggestion: integrate into alerting: compute region_spare = (available_gpus / total_gpus) * 100 and include in alert payload.

leah.sre: For the remediation playbook (manual path): 1) collect dmesg + nvml logs; 2) run memtest86 on card (offlined); 3) if memtest fails -> schedule RMA/replace; 4) if memtest passes -> try driver reboot and firmware check, re-enable.

kevin.ops: Add troubleshooting step: check power/PSU and ambient temps; high ECC sometimes from thermal or voltage instability.

jonathan.eng: For automation, I propose a 3-step auto-action with hysteresis: mark -> soft-migrate -> hard-drain. Mark after Band B for 1 hour, soft-migrate low-priority pods for 10min, if still Band C then hard-drain. Soft-migrate should prefer ephemeral workloads.

maria.mlinfra: We must ensure autoscaler and placement respect soft-migrate labels; otherwise we'll just hit capacity again. I'll add placement constraints 'drain_candidate=true' for low-priority queues.

leah.sre: Edge-case: simultaneous spikes across multiple racks — could indicate host firmware bug or fabric issue. If >10% of region is in Band B/C within 30m, escalate to infra-leads for coordinated investigation and consider throttling new GPU allocations.

kevin.ops: Also watch for pattern: ECC spike followed by Xid errors. If Xid appears after an ECC burst, escalate to hardware replace immediately.

jonathan.eng: Agree. We should add correlation rules: if Xid_count > 0 within 1h of ECC spike on same GPU -> immediate drain + replace flag.

maria.mlinfra: Who owns implementing the normalized_deg and region gating in alerting? I can take the prom rules + Grafana panels.

leah.sre: I'll own the runbook updates and oncall training. Kevin, can you prototype the soft-migrate workflow in the next week?

kevin.ops: Yep, I'll draft a simple controller that labels pods and triggers evictions for low-priority queues.

sre-bot: Action created: ECC-Playbook-2026-03 • Owner: leah.sre • Tasks: update runbook, add gating thresholds, oncall handbook.

deploy-bot: Note: any auto-drain changes must go through canary in staging before prod enablement.

jonathan.eng: Also add a reporting metric: weekly RMA_count_by_model and mean_time_between_ecc_spike per model, for procurement decisions.

kevin.ops: Summary of immediate actions: (1) Add normalized_deg prom rule (maria), (2) implement soft-migrate prototype (kevin), (3) runbook + training (leah), (4) add alert payload region_spare (sre-bot).

leah.sre: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to lock thresholds and auto-drain gating policies. Who can make it at 11:00 UTC?

maria.mlinfra: I can.

jonathan.eng: I can do 11:00 UTC.

kevin.ops: In.

leah.sre: Great. Closing thread — we'll use the meeting to finalize actionables. :white_check_mark:
